attribution.note: Marcus's own line in his signed Substack letter. He cites the Guardian/People's Daily as his basis, but the claim that China is eager is his own assertion.

semantics.note: Firm present-tense observation. 'Eager to collaborate on AI' is a fair rendering of 'practically begging' in an AI context. Treating the rebuttal of 'would never want to' as part of the claim fits the surrounding text.

contract.note: The plain reading (authoritative public Chinese appeals for bilateral AI cooperation, September 1–23) is ordinary and matches the evidence Marcus offered. It does not demand a measurable intensity or private sincerity, which is fair to the hyperbole.

evidence.note: People's Daily front-page piece dated 2026-09-22, inside the window. It explicitly urges using the intergovernmental AI dialogue and making AI a new frontier of China-US cooperation. This is an authoritative CCP public appeal.

Official MFA transcript dated 2026-09-22 (the 'company_disclosure' label is a misnomer). The spokesperson deflected questions on specific AI measures. This limits any inference of concrete commitments but does not rebut the public invitation.

reviews.rationale: The support condition is met. An authoritative CCP outlet's front page on Sept 22, 2026 actively called for bilateral AI cooperation with the US through the intergovernmental dialogue. The MFA deflection on specifics does not show China rejected cooperation or that the appeal was misrepresented. 'Practically begging' is rhetorical intensity, and the contract fairly scores only the active public appeal.
